instruction.text: Read the definitions of two types of cloning and assign their names and examples accordingly.

hint.text:
reproductive – relating to reproduction, i.e. the creation of babies or young plants
therapeutic – relating to the treatment of diseases
hint.sound: Reproductive means relating to reproduction, i.e. the creation of babies or young plants. Therapeutic means relating to the treatment of diseases.
hint.label: Vocabulary

atoms.b: Although reproductive cloning is already scientifically ((possible)), it is not legal to clone humans anywhere in the world. The cloning of ((animals)) is sometimes allowed, for example, for species conservation.

Therapeutic cloning is ((legal)) in some countries under strict guidelines. However, it is still highly controversial. The process requires ((stem)) cells taken from either adult humans or human embryos.

instruction.text: Decide whether the statements are true or false.
instruction.sound: Decide whether the statements are true or false.

atoms.a: Reproductive cloning is done for medical purposes.
Therapeutic cloning is a controversial topic.
Stem cells are used for therapeutic cloning.
Stem cells can be taken either from adults or embryos.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

hint.sound: <lang xml:lang='en-GB'>IVF</lang> steht für <lang xml:lang='en-GB'>in vitro fertilisation</lang> und bedeutet künstliche Befruchtung.
hint.label: IVF

atoms.text: Embryonic stem cells have special properties: they can turn into any kind of other cell. Adults also have stem cells, but they are limited in the types of cells they can turn into.

atoms.a: Which cells have a wider range of usage for medical purposes?

atoms.text: An egg cell can only turn into an embryo and begin producing stem cells after it has been fertilised. The embryos used for stem cell research are usually left over from IVF treatments. Extracting stem cells kills the embryo.

atoms.a: Which condition has to be met for the production of embryonic stem cells?
b: ++An egg cell has to be fertilised.
The embryo has to be implanted in a person's uterus.
The cells have to die first.
++If embryos are considered alive human beings, the procedure could be viewed as murder.
Therapeutic cloning of stem cells is not always guaranteed to work.

instruction.text: Decide whether the arguments are for or against the therapeutic cloning of embryonic stem cells.

hint.text: After IVF treatments, embryos can be kept in a frozen state for a long time. If the parent decides to have more children later, the embryo can be unfrozen and implanted in their uterus. This practice is only legal in some countries, such as the UK and the US.
hint.label: frozen embryos
